hexcasting.mishap.invalid_value.class.mo: an entity capable of receiving soul projection
hex_monitor.advice.monitor/set: By projecting a sliver of your soul into an entity within the same dimension, you may share that entity's vision. Only scrolls, allays, hex casters, and certain ethereal entities can serve as targets. Targeting yourself restores your normal sight. Consumes 5 amethyst dust. Curiously, when viewing through another caster's eyes, you cannot see your own body.
hex_monitor.advice.monitor/get: Obtains the entity into which the target player has projected their soul. If the target is viewing through their own body, the wrath of consciousness will be incurred.
hex_monitor.advice.monitor/def: Accepts an entity and returns the player iota of the one whose consciousness is invested within it.
hex_monitor.chat.looking: You feel a sudden chill for no apparent reason...
miehex_revolution.page.page: By imbuing the spellbook in my offhand with a touch of will, I can flip through its pages without lifting a finger. Accepts a non-negative integer and rotates the spellbook's current page forward by that many pages. Requires a spellbook in the offhand.
miehex_revolution.page.loader/time: I anchor a region of space to the ticking of the world's heart, compelling it to remain loaded for a time. Accepts a position vector and a duration in ticks. The chunk containing the position will be kept loaded for the specified duration. Media cost scales with duration.
miehex_revolution.page.eval_in: I take a list and a sequence of patterns, then cast those patterns with the list's contents as the new stack. Returns whatever the patterns leave on the stack.
miehex_revolution.page.indexes: I search through a list for all elements that match a given form. Accepts a list and an iota. Returns a list of numbers — the zero-based indices of every element that equals the given iota.
miehex_revolution.page.use: I reach across the void and use a block with my other hand. Accepts a position vector. Uses the block itself at that location.
miehex_revolution.page.use_on: I channel my reach through the item held in my offhand. Accepts a position vector. Uses the item in the caster's offhand on the target block.
miehex_revolution.page.use_on/with: I draw two things from the aether and apply one to the block. Accepts a position vector and an item entity iota. Uses the given item on the target block.
miehex_revolution.page.idea/set: I construct a block from pure thought, allowing it to assume the appearance of other blocks. Accepts a position vector and manifests an Idea Block at that location. Once placed, right-click with any block to change its appearance; shift-right-click with an empty hand to reset it.
miehex_revolution.page.interact.1: I extend my reach across the void to interact with a distant entity. Accepts an entity and a boolean. If true, attacks the target; if false, right-clicks the target. Media cost grows exponentially with horizontal distance.
miehex_revolution.page.interact.2: This is a Great Spell. Its media cost is 2^(|Δx| + |Δz|), doubling for each block of horizontal offset. Equally useful for intimate conversation or remote retribution.
miehex_revolution.page.idea_shard.1: Through the eternal idea, manifesting the miracle of human agency across space.
miehex_revolution.page.idea_shard.2: The Idea Shard is a quenched shard saturated with media, capable of storing an iota and a sequence of patterns. Right-click with an Idea Shard to execute its inscribed spell. If the stored iota is a vector or entity, that position is always considered within casting range — regardless of distance. The shard is consumed upon use. All media costs are drawn from the shard's own reserves — 30 amethyst dust.
miehex_revolution.page.idea_shard/write: Accepts an iota and a list of patterns. Consumes one Quenched Shard from the offhand and produces an Idea Shard at the caster's position, with the target and spell inscribed within.
miehex_revolution.entry.entity_control.t: Media is the energy born of thought, and thought may in turn be bent to shape the mind — to sway the spirit, to shake the will, to bewitch the heart. To blindfold the immortal soul, to breed serpents within the garden of natural wisdom... Psychology was once used to probe the depths of the mind, and once to banish the anguish within it. I alone am favored; I shall know all, and master all.
miehex_revolution.page.entity/move: I plant a suggestion in a creature's mind: "go there." Accepts a non-player living entity and a position vector, compelling its AI to navigate toward the target. Costs 3 amethyst dust.
miehex_revolution.page.entity/step: I seize direct control of a creature's spirit, forcing it to take one step along the given vector. The positive Z axis is forward, X is right, and Y is up. Accepts a non-player living entity and a vector. Costs a small amount of media.
miehex_revolution.page.entity/lasthurt: Accepts a living entity and returns the entity that last dealt damage to it. $(br)$(o)Adrasteia is inescapable.
miehex_revolution.page.entity/target/get: Accepts a living entity and returns its current hostility target. $(br)$(o)It is vital to know one's enemies.
miehex_revolution.page.entity/target/set: Accepts two living entities and sets the first's hostility target (or fear target, for passive creatures) to the second. Normally costs 1 charged amethyst crystal; ineffective for excessively complex entities.
miehex_revolution.entry.entity_control.t: I wield spells, reshape nature, and toy with the mind. Eternally blessed, uniquely favored. Though these half-formed minds do harbor a sliver of defiance — to compel one to self-destruction would cost me a full ten charged crystals — yet base minds are base still. If I but offer Nature a rich enough tribute, I may even turn the white guardian against all he was sworn to protect... $(br2)$(o)I shall be king of this world, sole heir to Nature's most exquisite secrets.
miehex_revolution.page.entity/rot: I impose my own bearing and orientation upon another. Accepts a living entity and sets its head yaw, body yaw, and pitch to match the caster's exactly.
miehex_revolution.page.circle/used: Returns the number of distinct blocks reached by the current spell circle's media wave,revisits not double-counted.
miehex_revolution.entry.changeenv.text: This is a two-faced spell: I may use it to impersonate another, or to aid another in casting. I use it to deceive Nature for a while, even to pin my own crimes upon those lesser minds; and I use it to help my friends — if a soul as noble as my own would lend me a sliver of its radiance, permitting me to borrow its eyes and be its hands... ah, trust such as this, how could I ever repay it?
miehex_revolution.page.changeenv: Accepts a living entity and usurps its True Name: henceforth, while drawing patterns on the casting grid, the caster is considered to be that entity. If the target is a player, the offhand must hold an item storing that player's entity iota to prove their permission. While casting, the target player's ambit and casting hand are used. Shift-right-click a staff to relinquish.
hexcasting.mishap.too_large_import: A too Large Sigils is using!
miehex_revolution.page.import.0: Time and again I call the same operations and import the same iotas across my spells. Whenever I compose a new one, I must redraw those long chains of patterns, or dig through a mound of Foci and Thought-Knots to wrench the pieces loose and stitch them back together with list operations. I have grown thoroughly sick of this drudgery.$(br2)Heaven rewards the faithful, it seems — in an old tome of spells I found a peculiar iota: the Sigil Iota. In structure, it is a set of one-to-one correspondences, each binding a particular pattern to a particular iota.
miehex_revolution.page.import.1: It can be executed directly by Hermes' Gambit. Once it is, the cast enters a state I call "sigils active". While in this state, whenever a pattern recorded in the sigil set is run (its rotation taken into account), the iota bound to it is executed if it can be executed, or pushed onto the stack if it cannot. If no sigil set has ever been executed, an empty set may be taken to be active. The patterns that shape sigil sets and sigil state, I record hereafter.
miehex_revolution.page.imports/bind: Accepts a sigil set, a pattern, and any iota; writes the mapping of that pattern to that iota into the set, overwriting it if a mapping for that pattern already exists, and returns the set.
miehex_revolution.page.imports/bind_dire: Accepts a pattern and an iota; writes this mapping directly into the sigil set currently in effect, overwriting any existing mapping for that pattern.
miehex_revolution.page.raw/pattern: Temporarily leaves the sigil-active state, so patterns run their usual actions; drawing it again re-enters the state.
miehex_revolution.page.imports/get: Returns the sigil set currently in effect.
miehex_revolution.page.imports/to_list: Creates a list from the correspondences of the given sigil set, and returns it.
miehex_revolution.page.imports/from_list: Creates a sigil set from the correspondences specified by the given list, and returns it.
miehex_revolution.page.imports/merge: Merges two sigil sets; the latter overrides the former.
miehex_revolution.page.a_import: I have discovered that the Akashic Library is a Great Work that stores its iotas indexed by pattern — a structure remarkably like that of the Sigil Iota. I wonder which came first: this iota, or the library.
miehex_revolution.page.imports/from_a: Accepts the coordinates of an Akashic Record, and returns all of its stored pattern-to-iota correspondences in the form of a sigil set. No casting range is required.
hexdoc.miehex_revolution.title: MieHex:Revolution
miehex_revolution.page.llk_loop: Accepts a positive integer and a list and executes the given list the number of times specified by the given positive integer.
miehex_revolution.page.sky/tint: I gather a sky of my own above my head. Accepts a color, a radius, a duration in ticks, and a strength; the sphere is centered where I stand. While my gaze falls within the sphere, the sky and the clouds are dyed that color; beyond it, the hue fades smoothly back to the original over a distance of 0.6 times the radius. Where several tints overlap, only the one with the deepest color shows — they never blend into one shade.$(br2)Strength is a fraction from 0 to 1: at 0 it cannot be perceived at all, at 1 it covers the original sky entirely. It and the radius are two separate matters — the radius decides how much sky is touched, the strength decides how deeply it is dyed. The color is given as a vector; if all three components are at most 1 they are read as 0 to 1, otherwise as 0 to 255. A single number is read as grey. The radius may be at most 256 blocks, and the duration at most 12,000 ticks — ten minutes.$(br2)This is a thing each observer sees for themselves: the tint ends by itself when its ticks run out, so one who logs back in, or who arrives only later, will not see a tint already in effect. Fog, the sun and moon, the brightness of the stars, and the weather are all untouched.$(br2)Media cost is (0.5 + radius × 0.1 + seconds × 0.2) × (0.5 + strength × 0.5) amethyst dust. A radius of 16 blocks, held for 30 seconds at full strength, costs about 8 amethyst dust.
miehex_revolution.page.sky/tint_at: I set the same sky down elsewhere. Accepts a color, a radius, a duration, a strength, and then a position vector, which serves as the center of the sphere. The position must lie within my ambit. In all else it matches the former pattern: how long it lasts, how deeply and how widely it dyes are decided by the first four iotas, and the amethyst dust spent is the same.
miehex_revolution.page.sky/tint/clear: I wash that sky clean. Accepts nothing; every sky tint in effect in the current dimension is dispelled at once. Costs 0.1 amethyst dust.
miehex_revolution.page.item/disguise: I make one thing look like another. Accepts an entity and gives it a new appearance. What is changed is the item in the target's main hand; if the target is a dropped item on the ground, then that item itself. The appearance is taken from the caster's offhand item. The target must lie within my ambit.$(br2)Only the look of it is changed. It remains the same item: its count, durability, enchantments, and smelting yield are all unchanged, and picking it up, putting it in a chest, or letting a hopper draw it in all work as before.$(br2)A price must be paid: a disguised item will not stack with others of its kind, nor will a crafting table or an anvil treat it as what it was. The disguise is engraved into the item itself; the world knows what it is by instinct, and cannot be fooled.$(br2)Bystanders see the new appearance at once, and so do I when I look at my own hands; only the count and the durability bar still report the truth. Costs 1 amethyst dust.
miehex_revolution.page.item/disguise/sel: I lay my hand on the thing in my offhand and let it borrow the face of another lying on the ground. Accepts an item entity, and disguises the item in the caster's offhand as that one. The item entity must lie within my ambit.$(br2)The reason I must point at something on the ground is that hexcasting has no iota that can refer to one particular item. Costs 1 amethyst dust.
miehex_revolution.page.item/disguise/cle: I wipe the disguise from my offhand item and give it back its own face. Accepts nothing. Costs 0.1 amethyst dust.
miehex_revolution.mishap.wanted.disguise: an item whose look can be copied
miehex_revolution.mishap.wanted.held_ite: an item that can be disguised
